sources.decision: Activation, quality and ablation are distinct signals. Only tool_used Skill graders are excluded from the without-arm by default, so agent activation uses arm: with-only. Plugin MCP servers do not start: mocks under evals/**/mocks/<server>/ with a saved tools/list make plugin tools observable.
Frontmatter and invocation rules are part of the product. disable-model-invocation blocks the Skill tool, so such a skill is evaluated through a prompt that starts with /plugin:skill.
Tools define the agent's declared capabilities; plugin agents ignore hooks and permissionMode, so file-writing tools cannot be path-limited and design agents are read-only.
The --max-budget-usd limit is estimated; it does not guarantee an exact billed amount.
HTTPX does not start lifespan on its own.
Required/nullable behavior, TypeError and serialization change in v2.
A session represents a transaction; roll back after a failed flush.
Use one AsyncSession per task and avoid implicit I/O when reading attributes.
Autogenerate requires review and does not infer renames; check shares its limits.

redundancyReview.finding: They share contract rules and produce guidance, a contract document and code respectively. The designer is read-only and returns its document in the response.
They share fixture/rollback guidance; the agent only writes tests and the caller executes them. The skill supports the verification workflow.
The skill guides persistence changes; reviewers only inspect and separate DDL from execution/sessions.
Diagnosis, authorized load generation and static inspection are distinct interventions. None establishes performance on its own.
The skill can guide changes and checks; the read-only agent returns a design. Avoid imposing layers/import-linter.
Deployment concerns overlap; implementation guidance, read-only review and pipelines have different triggers.
HTTP contract design differs from consumer/provider verification and release gates.
